newsitem.title: USA: City settles U.S. housing discrimination charges.
newsitem.headline: City settles U.S. housing discrimination charges.

text.p: The city of Waukegan, Ill. agreed to pay $200,000 in damages and fines to settle U.S. charges that it violated a federal law barring housing discrimination, the U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday.
Justice had accused the city of abridging the Fair Housing Act by enacting a code that limits the number of Hispanic family members living together, the department said in a statement.

The city had permitted only a husband and wife, their children, and no more than two additional relatives to live in a home or apartment, regardless of its size, Justice said. The city used the restriction to discriminate against Hispanics, Justice charged.
Under an agreement approved by the U.S. District Court in Chicago, Waukegan will stop restricting the number of people living in a house based on the occupants' relationships.
